# 2004-12-04 run 04 — Coach's assessment

Next game: at NYI, Mon 2004-12-06. TOR 18-5-0-2 (40 pts, 10 straight wins, last 10 at 7.5 GF / 1.8 GA a night) vs NYI 12-10-1-1, 27 pts, last 10 at 2.5 GF / 3.3 GA (q27, q44). First meeting of the season — 4 left in the series (q35).

**Phase 1 — COMPLETE. Phase 2 — COMPLETE. Phase 3 — COMPLETE.**

## Phase 1 — Development: is every U23 getting the games he has earned?

### Getting them — no action

- **Gaborik (22)** — 25/25 games, 18.4 a night, 34 points, second line and power play. Fully used.
- **Klesla (22), Upshall (21), Eminger (21), Alexeev (22), Spezza (21)** — 22 to 25 games all. In and staying in.
- **Nash (20)** — 25 games, 12.9 a night on the third line, 22 points. The right dose for a 20-year-old holding a bottom-six job and producing.
- **Chlup (18)** — 14 games at 11.1 a night, third-line centre. The games-played gap is injury — return date Dec 3rd (q25), so he's back for Monday. Third line is the right bench for him: real minutes while Sundin carries the top. One flag: morale 82, lowest of the young group on a ten-game winner; ice time is the lever besides winning, and he sits at the useful-player band. His minutes should climb now he's healthy.
- **Colaiacovo (21)** — 10 games, but return date Dec 1st (q29). When in he skates 18.7 a night on the second pair, first kill, second power play. Fully trusted, not underused.
- **Koltsov (23)** — 11 games, 9.3 a night, **12 points — 1.09 a game** (q26). Out-scoring his minutes by a mile. Not breaking the fourth line tonight — it was set deliberately — but he's the first man up if it goes quiet.

### Not getting them — and honest about it

- **Smirnov (19, LW)** — zero games, and what I can see does not say he has earned any yet. Scratch is correct.
- **Safronov (23, D)** — zero games, healthy, five defencemen ahead of him producing. My problem is solved without him, but 23 and shelved is an asset going sour — GM's side of the wall; the plan should say so either way.
- **Spacek (19, C)** — 11 games at 16.0 a night, then off the dressing list with nothing in the injury column (q31). Not putting him back Monday on a hunch mid-streak, but I want to know what changed before I plan around him.
- **Chistov (21, LW)** — healthy, no injury record, scratched, 14 games at 9.5, 4 points. Standing problem; at 21 with the club's opinion on file, scratch-bench is wasting him.

**Phase 1 decisions:** Dress Chistov for NYI — development. Koltsov stays put, first promotion if the fourth line goes quiet — development. Give Chlup his shifts back now he's healthy — his 82 morale is the room's soft spot and ice time is the fix. Rest of the group right in both directions; Smirnov and Safronov have earned nothing yet and the scratches are correct.

## Phase 2 — Roles and units

- **Six defencemen suit and all six dress** (McCabe–Kaberle, Fischer–Colaiacovo, Klesla–Eminger). Svehla (428 minutes this season) and Tucker dress nowhere; that is the settled shutdown-surplus plan and it still stands — no role for them the current six doesn't fill.
- **Goalies:** Belfour is 9-1, 2.57, .907 with 3 shutouts (q39) but was carrying an injury with a return date of Dec 5th (q40) — one day before puck-down at the Islanders. My call: **Belfour starts if he's right; Aebischer (9-3, 3.24/.879, who backstopped the last six straight, q42) starts if there's any doubt.** I'll make it at the rink on his health.
- **Power play:** the Dec 4 decision — Gaborik up to the first unit — is still not on the sheet; he's showing on the second unit (q23). Gaborik has 34 points; put him on PP1 before face-off. Richards' unit stays as is behind it.
- **Faceoffs:** Sundin and Richards keep all draw duty. Their centre depth is beatable — Bates (81/158) is the only draw man they dress up the middle, Papineau 53/114, Scatchard 31/67 (q37). Below our vets we still have the faceoff cliff — Chlup at 75 and 18 — so no schematic juggling tonight.

## Phase 3 — Matchup vs NYI

- **The headline: Alexei Yashin is not in their lineup.** He's on their roster (25 pts in 16 GP, 1.56 a game, healthy, morale 94) but not dressed into any line (q37, q41, q45). Their top centre tonight is Shawn Bates. Their scoring without Yashin: Blake 33, Parrish 29, Hamrlik 28 (q37).
- **Shift matching:** their penalty kill runs Bates with K. Timander, and Mapletoft's unit second. Our top two centres have the skill against those units and against their third pairing — keep Sundin's and Richards' lines on the ice when that traffic is over the boards. No names move; just whose shifts land against whose.
- **Their blue line logs heavy minutes** — Aucoin 30.5, Hamrlik 27.3 a night (q37) — and they're a middling team in decline (2.5 goals a game over the last ten). Gaborik and Mogilny against that mileage is our best path; keep the second line pressing their first pair rather than hiding from it.
- **Our even-strength lines do not change.** Ten straight, 7.5 a goal a night, 1.8 against. You do not touch that order two nights after a 6-0 and a 13-0 (q42), and the Islanders are missing their best player. The only moves: Chistov in as an extra body, Gaborik to PP1, and the goalie call above.
- **Locker room:** morale runs 82-100 on a ten-game winner — the winning is doing the work. Chlup's 82 is the only soft spot and his fix is shifts, not coddling.

## Bottom line for the GM

No lineup surgery — we're on a ten-game run and they're missing Yashin. Dress Chistov (development), get Gaborik onto the first power-play unit per the Dec 4 call (it isn't on the sheet yet), and Belfour starts if his knock is cleared, otherwise Aebischer. Koltsov is the man up if the fourth line goes quiet.

All recommendations recorded r1-r11.

Phase 1 complete: dress Chistov (development), Koltsov promotion watch, Chlup minutes up, no other changes. Phase 2 complete: Belfour start pending health, Gaborik to PP1, blue line as-is. Phase 3 complete: no even-strength changes vs a Yashin-less Islanders team; shift-match top nine vs their second kill. Recommendations r1-r14 recorded. Activation phases finished; GM message sent covering all three.

---

# Phase 2 — Roles

## Q1: Is each unit built from players who suit it?

**Even strength — the four lines are built right.**

- **L1 (Sundin/Roberts/Mogilny, McCabe/Fischer):** checking mean 79 with best 92 — this is a skilled top line that can still forecheck. Roberts at CHKG 90 (q49) is the anchor that lets Sundin and Mogilny play with the puck. Right build.
- **L2 (Richards/Gaborik/Afinogenov, Kaberle/Colaiacovo):** a scoring line — speed best 99, scoring best 93. You don't ask a second scoring unit to be a checking unit; its job is goals, and it has four of our top-five shooters on it (q49). Right build.
- **L3 (Chlup/Upshall/Nash, Klesla/Eminger):** checking mean 79, and Nash at 83 with Klesla 81 and Eminger 86 — a genuine middle-six grind line with a young centre learning in front of them. Right build.
- **L4 (Spezza/Koltsov/Alexeev):** checking mean 60 — deliberately so. That's the speed unit, set Dec 4; best speed 96, playmaking mean 77 on a fourth line is unusual in a good way. The one wrinkle: Spezza is 26 of 81 in the draws this season — **32%** (q48). He is a minus-19 faceoff man on a line whose job is not to win draws but to change games with pace. Smaller tool: on the kill and in their end we should be leaning on Richards and Upshall for the important draws, not scheming Spezza off his line.

**Faceoff duty is honestly stated across the sheet:** Sundin 73% won this season, Richards 67% (q48). Between those two we give up very few draws. The third string is the problem — see Q2.

**Power play:**
- **P1 (Sundin/Roberts/Mogilny, McCabe/Kaberle):** shoots 92, 94, 89 across the front — no one is hiding a soft wrist shot (q49). This unit can score on its own. **But the Dec 4 decision still hasn't landed: Gaborik belongs on this unit.** His shot grade is 92 with 93 accuracy — second only to Mogilny on the roster (q49) — and his 34 points say it louder than any grade. Smallest possible intervention: he comes on for McCabe (shot 88, and McCabe's real value is the point shot and the kill, which he keeps on PP2's rival and K2). That costs one rep of first-unit timing between McCabe's point and Sundin's net-front — cheap this early in a season, and we've decided it was worth it once already.
- **P2 (Richards/Fischer, Colaiacovo, Alexeev/Gaborik):** Richards 86 shot, Fischer 84 — enough bite with Gaborik until he moves up. Fine as the second unit.

**Penalty kill:**
- **K1 (Fischer/Colaiacovo, Roberts/Gaborik):** Fischer 90 checking, Roberts 90 — this is a first kill with two real penalty killers and two mobile forwards. Right build.
- **K2 (Kaberle/McCabe, Richards/Upshall):** Upshall carries CHKG 87 (q49) — the hidden reason the second kill works. Right build.

## Q2: Does the roster hold enough of each role?

- **Shutdown defence: no shortage — a surplus.** We dress six defencemen and bench Tucker (CHKG 92) and Svehla (92, and SHPW 88 besides). The problem is the opposite of the usual one: two of our three best checkers have no role the current six leaves them. That's the settled plan and it still holds — I'd rather be short on ice for two honest defenders than short on either.
- **Third-line faceoff winner: a genuine roster gap, and I'll name it plainly.** The centre depth chart in the draws is Sundin 90, then Richards 70 and Chlup 75 — an 18-year-old is our third-ranked draw man. Among every TOR forward with real reps this season, nobody but Sundin and Richards is above 63% (q48). Tonight it's covered — their centres are beatable — but in a playoff series against a true checking centre I have no one to send over the puck but Mats. I'm not asking for "a centre"; I'm asking you to know that **a third-line faceoff winner (the FACE 80-ish kind) is the one role on this roster no arrangement of it produces.** It's not fixable by moving names.
- **Shooting, speed, clutch, stamina:** inventory is deep — four 89+ shots, four 92+ skaters, Sundin/Mogilny/Roberts/Kaberle all 90+ clutch. No gap.
- **Toughness:** best 73 (Roberts/McCabe) with Tucker's 70 on the bench. Nobody on this roster is an enforcer; the four 89+ checkers are how we substitute for that — honest, and enough while they stay healthy.

## Phase 2 verdict

Units suit their jobs. The only composition change is the one already decided and not yet executed — **Gaborik to PP1**, cost: one rep of McCabe-Sundin point timing, worth it. The one roster problem is the **third faceoff winner**, and that's yours, not mine.

---

# Phase 3 — Matchup: at NYI, Mon 2004-12-06

## Honest read of them

- **Missing their best player, visibly.** Yashin — 25 points in 16 games — dresses into no line (q41, q45). In his place, Shawn Bates centres the first line. **Correction to what I said earlier today: Bates is no gimme** — FACE 94, checking 83, speed 93. He's an honest first-line centre. Their centre depth *behind* him is where the soft spot lives: Papineau 66 on the draw, Mapletoft 62. Scatchard (84 FACE, 89 CHKG, TOUG 85) is a real third-centre and our weak spot at L3C is an 18-year-old.
- **Their power play is the worst in the league: 2 for 57 — 3.5%** (q50). Dead last of thirty clubs. They've been shorthanded at a record rate and converted twice. Meanwhile our penalty kill has conceded 3 short-handed goals all season in 25 games (q51). The special-teams edge Monday is entirely ours and costs us nothing to take.
- **Their goaltending is the attack plan.** DiPietro starts: rebound control 66, intelligence 73, short-sides 70 (brief grades) — a 23-year-old who flakes when there's a body in front and second chances. We dress four forwards who shoot 90+ (q49). This is a game to shoot — 147 goals in 25 games says we will (q27).
- **Their top pair is old and heavy on miles** — Aucoin 31, Hamrlik 30 — but their endurance grades (99 and 97) say they don't visibly fade, and both are fit for Monday (brief flags). The case for pressing them is skill and youth against them, not chasing wind.
- **One trap: Chris Simon.** TOUG 95, penalties-drawn 95, on their third line. Our two most injury-prone staples — Sundin and McCabe — must stay on their feet around him. No embellishment, finish through contact. Coaching point, no lineup change.

## What changes for THIS opponent — and what doesn't

**Matchup-driven (reason: matchup):**
1. **Shoot to rebound, attack the net-front.** All four lines, but especially Sundin's and Gaborik's — second chances are DiPietro's kryptonite (REBC 66). This is a how-we-play call, no names move.
2. **Draw assignment: Richards, not Chlup, takes the dots against Scatchard** whenever the third lines meet. Chlup is 18 and 75 on the draw; Scatchard is 84 with 85 toughness and will eat a teenager on the dot and start rushes off it. Sundin-Bates is the fair fight and I welcome it. No composition change — just who steps in.
3. **Top nine on the ice against their P2 and their third pair** — Papineau's 58 checking and Hawgood's 60 are the softest real minutes on their sheet (brief). Shift matching only.

**Decided for other reasons — not to be confused with matchup (reason: development):**
4. Chistov dresses as the 13th forward — that's the development call from Phase 1; against a Yashin-less Islanders team it happens to cost nothing, but it was made for him, not for them.
5. Gaborik to PP1 — Dec 4 decision, phase 2. Against the league's worst PK unit (q50) it's doubly right, but the reason is his 34 points and 92/93 shot, not their weakness.

**Goalie:** Belfour returns Dec 5 and starts Monday — 9-1, 2.57, .907, and the higher grades on the sheet at every position that matters against a team we outplay 7.5 goals to 2.5 (q44). The promise I made the GM stands: **Aebischer gets the first game after this one.**

**What does NOT change: everything else.** Ten straight, 7.5 for and 1.8 against, opponent missing 25 points of centre, league-worst power play coming to our 3-SHGA kill. "No change" is the answer for the even-strength order, and it's not laziness, it's the matchup.

## Phase 3 verdict

Play our game harder at their weakest points: rebounds off DiPietro, draws against their bottom-six centres, top nine on their soft pair. One correction I owe the GM from this morning: their replacement centre Bates is good — I won't sell the top of their order short. Lines unchanged; Chistov, Gaborik-PP1 and Belfour are the only sheet changes, and two of the three were decided before I looked at New York.

---

# Activation closeout — 2004-12-04 run 04

Phase 1 (development): COMPLETE. Phase 2 (roles): COMPLETE. Phase 3 (matchup): COMPLETE.

Recommendations recorded: r1–r18 covering every GREEN duty — development_opportunity, ice_time, faceoffs, morale_watch, role_composition, line_recommendations, opponent_matchup. RED duties (development_trends, per_game_performance) not attempted.

Final card for Monday at NYI:
1. Dress Chistov as extra forward — development (r3, r12).
2. Gaborik onto the first power-play unit — the Dec 4 decision, finally executed (r1, r16).
3. Belfour starts if his Dec 5 return holds; Aebischer starts the next game as promised (r18).
4. Game plan: shoot at DiPietro's rebounds; Richards covers Scatchard on the dot; top nine onto their second unit and third pair (r17).
5. No even-strength line changes (r13, r16). Koltsov is first man up if the fourth line goes quiet (r4).
6. Roster gap flagged to the GM: no third-line faceoff winner exists on this roster (r15).

Postscript from the fixture list (q52): NYI Mon Dec 6, then NEW JERSEY at home Tue Dec 7 — a back-to-back to open the week. That makes the goalie plan clean: Belfour Monday if he's right, Aebischer Tuesday against New Jersey exactly as promised, and neither man runs the second night of a back-to-back on one day's rest. Belfour is 39; the schedule is making my decision for me and it agrees with the promise.

# 2004-12-04 — run 03

Next game: Monday 2004-12-06, at New York (Islanders). Club has played 25.

---

## Phase 1 — development: is every young guy getting the games he has earned?

### The calendar first (this reframes the whole table)

The GP column is frozen for some of these men because of injuries, not because
of a coach's decision. Injuries on our list with a return date (q21):

- Carlo Colaiacovo — back **December 1st**
- Mats Sundin — back **December 2nd**
- Petr Chlup — back **December 3rd**
- Ed Belfour — back **December 5th**

And the club's record since the start of November is a perfect 10-0-0 at
7.5 goals for, 1.8 against (q33). 10 games. That is exactly the gap between
"10 GP" and "25 GP", exactly the gap between "11 GP" and "25 GP", exactly the
gap between "14 GP" and "25 GP".

So the shares in the brief are **not** 0–56% of the games available. Smirnov's
0 games is 0 of 10. Spacek's 44% is 11 of 11. Chistov's 56% is 14 of 14.
Safronov's 0 games is 0 of 25, which is the only real one in that group.

I cannot say any of these men is or is not developing — I have two saves three
days apart and that is nothing. What I can say is who has been handed the
chance and who has not.

### Getting more than they have earned

**Rick Nash, 20 — 25 of 25, third-line left wing, 12.9 mpg, 22 points.**
Underserving of that. Mogilny is 39 points in 25 and Roberts 32 in 25, and
neither is ahead of Nash for ice (16.9 and 16.7 a night, q32/q30). Nash is
carrying more of the game than two men a full tier above him on production.
His 32 shots in 322 minutes is among the lowest rates of any forward on the
top three lines (only Upshall at 25 in 338 is under it, q32), which tells me
he is being used to forecheck and grind rather than to score, and a grinder's
role does not need 13 minutes out of a 20-year-old. Bring him back toward 10
and give the difference to the men who are being starved. Workload, not
development — I am not doing him a favour by shortening his night, I am
putting his minutes where they score.

**Rostislav Klesla, 22 — 25 of 25, 14.7 mpg, 13 points, +0.** Fine, he has
earned third-pair minutes. Leave him alone.

### Earning more than they are getting

**Petr Chlup, 18 — 14 of 14 since his return, third-line centre, 11.1 mpg,
8 points, 31 shots.** Two things matter. He has not missed a shift since the
injury — 14 appearances out of 14 games (q21, q32) — and he is taking and
winning real draws at 18 years old: 46 of 73 (q32), more faceoffs than Spezza
and Spacek combined. He is also the lowest-morale player on the club at 82
(q40), and he is the one young forward whose minutes are visibly under what
his game is worth. 11.1 a night is a useful-player number for a kid already
centreing a scoring line. **Development, and the fix is on Nash's side of the
sheet.**

**Konstantin Koltsov, 23 — 11 of 11 since his return, 9.3 mpg, 12 points in
102 minutes.** 12 points per 100 minutes is the best rate of any forward on
the roster — Mogilny is at 9.2 per 100, Sundin 8.3, Gaborik 7.4 (q32) — and
he is getting depth minutes on the fourth line. He has played every game he
has been healthy for and produced every night he has played.
**Development.** He belongs on the second line. (I checked before writing
this: he has taken no faceoffs this season, so nothing about him is justified
on draws — he earns this on the scoresheet.)

**Stanislav Chistov, 21 — 14 of 14 available, healthy, 4 points, dressing
every night without a line (q20).** The healthiest of the three and the only
one who has taken zero shifts. He has earned nothing yet on production, but
the club is 10-0-0 with a 1.8 goals-against a night and every close forward
is already at 25 games; this is the cheapest ice on the roster to find. Take
the minutes off Nash's line, do not disturb the top six. **Development.**

**Vaclav Spacek, 19 — 11 of 11 available, 16.0 mpg when he played, 6 points.**
Healthy now and back in the stands. He was getting top-nine minutes before the
injury. He and Chistov cannot both come in at once — one of them, at centre,
where Chlup is the man needing a partner rather than a rival. **Development,
one slot only.**

### Getting exactly what they have earned

**Colaiacovo, 21** — 18.7 mpg on the second pair since December 1st, back to
full workload. Earned. **Spezza, 21** — centre of the fourth line, 88% of the
schedule. Earned, and he is doing the job that line is for. **Upshall, 21** —
regular third-winger plus both penalty kills. Earned. **Eminger, 21** — 24 of
24, 15.0 mpg, third pair. Earned. **Gaborik, 22** — 34 points, 18.4 mpg, 71
shots, second right wing and the first penalty-kill centre. He has out-earned
every assignment on this list. **Alexeev, 22** — 25 of 25, fourth wing plus
the second power play. Earned.

### Not being wasted — being told no

**Vyacheslav Smirnov, 19** and **Kirill Safronov, 23** are both at 0 games
since the calendar turned (q32). Their morale reads 100, which is the team
winning talking, not the two of them being content.

- Smirnov: 0 points in 0 minutes, ceiling 70, the lowest of anyone on this
  list. He is a healthy scratch because he has not out-played anyone ahead of
  him, and that is the correct answer. I am not putting him in to make a
  number look kind.
- Safronov: 0 games all season. 23, defenceman, and there are six defencemen
  in front of him who are healthy right now — Fischer, Kaberle, McCabe,
  Colaiacovo, Klesla, Eminger, with Svehla and Salo also waiting (q20). He is
  not being wasted, he is blocked, and no arrangement of this blue line clears
  him this season. If he is still home in January we are carrying a defenceman
  we cannot use, and that is the GM's problem, not mine.

### What the young group adds up to

Every one of the ten regulars 23 or under is dressed and playing — except
Chistov, who dresses without a line, and the two who have not earned it.
There is no development crisis on this roster; there is a distribution
problem: one 20-year-old with more ice than his production justifies, and two
young forwards at 9–11 minutes who have each played every minute they were
healthy for. The minutes exist. I would rather find them there than disturb a
top six that is winning ten straight.

---

## Phase 2 — at New York, Monday December 6th

### What they are

12-10-1, 27 points, 95 for and 91 against — a .500-style hockey club that has
gone WWLLLLLWWL (q28). Not scaring anyone. Their two best defencemen, Aucoin
(88 checking) and Hamrlik (84), are both back — their return dates were
December 2nd and 3rd (q41) — so their first pair is intact again.

The big one: **Alexei Yashin is a healthy scratch** (q42). 25 points in 16
games, sitting. Their first line is Bates–Kvasha–Parrish with Aucoin/Hamrlik
behind it, and Bates is a 94 faceoff man (q44) — he will win his draws
against anyone on our roster except Sundin at 90. Their third line is the
nasty one: Scatchard 89 checking / 84 draws, flanked by Czerkawski and Simon
(q37, q44). Their first centre is Bates, not Yashin, and our first line is
Sundin's, so the opening-ice draw battle is roughly a wash; nobody is owed a
reshuffle for that.

No per-game lines exist, so I do not know who was in net for their last win
and I will not pretend otherwise.

### Our side

- Ten straight, 40 points, 147:76 (q35). Morale across the room is 68–100
  territory with only Aebischer (80) and Chlup (82) off the pace (q40).
- **Belfour is back** (returned December 5th, q21). Ten games, 2.57 goals
  against, .907, three shutouts, 9-1 — against Aebischer's 3.24 and .879
  (q36).
- We dress two of our three best checkers nowhere: Tucker 92 and Svehla 92
  sit (q45). That is a standing problem, not Monday's problem — New York
  hardly punishes it.

### The calls

**1. Belfour starts.** He is the best goalies we have on the numbers since
late October, he has had four days to shake the rust off, and we are on the
road against a team that is not going to outchance us. Aebischer gets New
Jersey Tuesday — back-to-back, and he has carried this streak while Ed was
out, which earns him the home game. Matchup/in-net, plain and simple.

**2. Koltsov to the second line, Chistov in on the fourth.** Koltsov leads
the club at 12 points per hundred minutes played (q32) and is on 9.3 a night
of fourth-line duty; Chistov is healthy, dressing without a line, and is the
one shirt on the rack. Afinogenov comes out — 14 points in 13 is good, but he
is the most recent man back from injury and the streak has no room for
sentiment. Top six untouched: this changes one winger on the second line and
one on the fourth. **Development.** If the GM wants zero risk against a
sub-.560 team, keeping the top six exactly as it is and simply running the
fourth line less is the fallback — but the top six doesn't move either way.

**3. Nothing else moves.** Lines that win ten straight stay. No strategy
tinkering — I will not name a system I cannot show him results for.

Queries: q28 (NYI record/form), q30 (our lines), q32 (our numbers), q36
(goalie records), q37/q38 (their lines and scoring), q41/q42 (their injuries
and scratches), q44/q45 (checking and faceoff grades both rooms), q35
(standings).

# 2004-12-04 — Run 02

Next game: at New York Islanders, 2004-12-06. We are 18-5-2 (40 pts, second in the league, on a ten-game
winning streak); they are 12-10-1 (27 pts), winners of two straight (q31 — their win_streak is 2; the
all-wins last-ten string is ours, theirs reads WWLLLLLWWL). (q18, q31)

## Phase 1 — Are the young guys getting the games they've earned?

We dress 12 forwards and 6 defencemen and every one of those slots is currently held by someone who is
producing, which is the whole story for this age group.

**Earning it, and getting it:**
- **Rick Nash** (20) — all 25, third line, 22 points. (q22)
- **Marian Gaborik** (22) — all 25, right wing on the second line, plus first-team faceoff and kill work,
  34 points, 71 shots — most on the club. He is not being hidden. (q22, q23)
- **Rostislav Klesla** (22), **Steve Eminger** (21) — 25 / 24 games, third defensive pairing together.
  Fine for their age. (q22)
- **Nikita Alexeev** (22) — all 25, fourth line and the second power-play unit. (q23)
- **Scottie Upshall** (21) — all 25, third line plus a kill unit. (q23)
- **Jason Spezza** (21) — 22 of 25, centre of the fourth line, 10 points. A checking role at his age is
  the right prescription, not a demotion.
- **Petr Chlup** (18) — 14 games after coming back Dec 3rd, centre of the third line, 8 points on 31
  shots. He's playing, and he's playing centre. For an 18-year-old that's the deal I want. (q21, q22)
- **Carlo Colaiacovo** (21) — 10 games because he was out until Dec 1st, now back on the second pairing
  with the second power-play unit and a kill unit. Fully in the lineup. (q21, q23)

**The two I'd argue about, and I'm not changing them before this game:**
- **Konstantin Koltsov** (23) — 12 points in 11 games, the best rate on the club per game played, and
  he's on the fourth line. He has earned top-nine minutes. I am still not moving him two days before a
  game we're favoured in: the second line of Richards — Afinogenov — Gaborik is producing (Afinogenov has
  14 in 13) and I don't break up a working line on a whim. First change if a forward gets knocked out.
  Reason class: development, with an honest nod that it probably helps us win too. (q22, q23)
- **Vaclav Spacek** (19) — 6 points in 11 games, healthy scratch with no line assignment. Closest call on
  the roster. But I'd be benching a productive forward to dress him — all twelve forwards up front are
  dressed and none are hurting. First in line the moment we lose someone.

**Not a grievance:**
- **Stanislav Chistov** (21) — 4 points in 14 games, 0.29 a game. The ceiling is what he might become;
  what he's giving us now does not beat any dressed wing. Stay down.
- **Kirill Safronov** (23) — zero games, but six defencemen are dressed, all healthy, all playing. He's
  the seventh defenceman in a six-man world.
- **Vyacheslav Smirnov** (19) — zero games and the lowest ceiling of the group. Not being wasted. He has
  not earned a spot and the ceiling alone doesn't buy one.

Everyone 23 or under who deserves a place has one. The ones without one either haven't earned it yet
(Smirnov, Chistov) or are behind a full, healthy, productive group (Spacek, Safronov).

## Phase 2 — Roles

### Unit fit
- **L1** — built right: best scoring unit, Sundin's 90 draws, and a 79 checking mean nobody asks less of a
  scoring line for. (role audit, q39)
- **L2** — a skill line by design; 68 checking mean is not a flaw when the job is creating, not containing.
- **L3** — the best balanced line on the club: Nash 83 and Upshall 87 checking, Chlup 75 on draws. (q39)
- **L4** — auditing it as a checking line fails it (60 mean, 52 draws) and fails honestly: Spezza, Koltsov
  and Alexeev are not checkers and cannot be arranged into one. Nash to the fourth and Upshall to the third
  buys 4 points of checking in the wrong direction and breaks a settled line. **Fix is usage, not
  composition:** L4 plays as a speed/transition unit, shutdown minutes go to L3 and the kill units. (q39)
- **P1/P2** — enough shooting and hands between them (Mogilny 94 scoring, Gaborik 92, Sundin, Kaberle);
  our 17.9% is a conversion problem, not a personnel problem. (q30, q39)
- **K1/K2** — both at 77 checking mean; the kills can kill. Gaborik on K1 is the only cost worth naming —
  our best skater burning stamina on the penalty kill — and against a 3.5% man-advantage it is affordable.

### Role sufficiency (roster problems, not lineup problems)
- **Checking: surplus, not gap.** Tucker 92 and Svehla 92 sit home while four dressed skaters carry 87+
  (q36, q37). They stay warm for the first injury.
- **Second/third-line centre: the real gap.** Sundin 90, then 75 (Chlup), 71 (Holden, scratched), 55
  (Spezza) — a cliff, not a depth chart (q39). Our bottom-two centres will lose most draws against any
  competent centre and no lineup arrangement fixes that. **GM item: a centre who can win a draw is the
  position of need** — ahead of "more grit", which we already have too much of.
- **No enforcer anywhere** (best toughness on the roster is Roberts at 73) — noted, not chased.

(3 of 29 skaters carry revised grades; everyone else is on shipped grades, and I've read them as such.)

## Phase 3 — Matchup: at NYI, Monday Dec 6th

**Honest read of them.** 12-10-1, 27 points, 95 for / 91 against — a middle hockey team that just won two
straight (q18, q31). We score 5.88 a game and give up 3.04; they score 3.96 and give up 3.79 (q30). On
what the season shows we are the better team by a wide margin; the risk Monday is the let-down spot, not
their roster.

**Their personnel (q26, q40, q41):**
- Top line Bates — Kvasha — Parrish behind Hamrlik — Aucoin. Bates is a real first centre (draws 94,
  speed 93); Parrish 29 points, Blake 33. Hamrlik and Aucoin both returned early December and are fit for
  Monday; Aucoin's 96 shot power is the one item to respect on their point.
- Their third line — Scatchard (89 checking, 85 toughness) with Chris Simon (95 toughness) — will try to
  make Monday ugly.
- In net: DiPietro starts, 10-7 at 3.57; Snow at 4.00 behind him (q28, q41). Neither has been sharp.
- Their power play is 2-for-57 (q30) — it barely exists. Peca (Jan 13) and Jonsson (Dec 16) remain out (q32).

**Centre-by-centre (q40, q39):** Bates 94 vs Sundin 90 — we lose that draw, win almost every other
conversation that line has. Scatchard 84 vs Chlup 75 — the kid will lose draws there; that's a changeover
problem, not a disaster, with Nash and Upshall behind him. Papineau 66 and Mapletoft 62 vs Richards 70
and Spezza 55 — even. Nobody to hide, nobody to attack with a special matchup.

**Decision: no change for this opponent** (matchup class, separate from the development items above):
- Their 3.5% power play gives no case to touch the kills; Gaborik can stay on the first kill without the
  usual stamina worry.
- Their physical third line is exactly what our third line is built for; Klesla/Eminger is the right
  answer, not a call-up of the scratched checkers.
- Our scoring depth against a 3.79-goals-against team is best met by keeping all four units intact.
- The Belfour start is a merit decision (return + GAA), reinforced — not driven — by DiPietro's 3.57.
- What I fear is us: ten-game winners, two days off, road game against a desperate two-game winner is the
  classic flat night. The answer to that is the same lineup with full stop, not a reshuffle.

Chemistry cost of the game plan: zero. Nothing moves.

## What I cannot see and did not pretend to

Skater ice time (nowhere in this data), morale as the game displays it, and how these kids have actually
progressed since October — two saves three days apart is not a trend. Workload talk is inferred from games
played and lineup slot. No per-game data, so nothing in here is about who did what on a given night.
